blocks.html: A shopkeeper keeps accounts in a ruled register: items in rows, quantity, rate and amount in columns. If one rate changes, every total must be worked out again by hand. A spreadsheet is an electronic register that does all the arithmetic automatically — change one number and every total updates instantly.
Definition: A spreadsheet is application software that organises data in rows and columns and performs calculations, analysis and charts on it.
Examples: Microsoft Excel, LibreOffice Calc (free), Google Sheets (online).
Uses: marks sheets and result analysis, family budgets, shop accounts, attendance registers, salary sheets, sales reports.

rows: An Excel file (extension .xlsx); it contains one or more worksheets
One page of rows and columns, shown as a tab at the bottom (Sheet1, Sheet2…)
A horizontal line of cells, numbered 1, 2, 3… (Excel has 1,048,576 rows)
A vertical line of cells, lettered A, B, C… Z, AA, AB… up to XFD (16,384 columns)
The box where a row and a column meet
The selected cell, shown with a thick border; its address appears in the Name Box
A block of cells written as first:last, e.g. B2:D4 (9 cells)
Shows the content or formula of the active cell
The small square at the bottom-right of the active cell; drag it to copy or continue a series

blocks.html: Types of data: text (labels such as names), numbers (marks, prices), dates and times, and formulas.
AutoFill: type Monday in a cell and drag the fill handle — Excel fills Tuesday, Wednesday… Type 1 and 2 in two cells, select both and drag — Excel continues 3, 4, 5…
A formula always starts with an equals sign =.
Excel follows the BODMAS order: brackets first, then powers, then × and ÷, then + and −. So =2+3*4 gives 14, but =(2+3)*4 gives 20.

Relative reference (A1 ): changes when the formula is copied. =SUM(B2:D2) in E2 becomes =SUM(B3:D3) when copied to E3. This is what we usually want.
Absolute reference ($A$1 ): stays fixed when copied. If cell H1 holds the maximum marks 300, write =E2/$H$1*100 so that every row divides by H1.
Mixed reference ($A1 or A$1 ): only the column or only the row is fixed.

blocks.html: Press F4 while typing a reference to switch between these forms.

items.html: Number formats — Currency (₹), Percentage (%), Date, decimal places.
Merge & Centre — joins cells for a title across the top.
Borders and fill colour, Wrap Text for long text, column width (double-click the column border to auto-fit).
Conditional formatting — changes a cell's colour by a rule, e.g. marks below 33 shown in red.
Freeze Panes (View tab) — keeps the heading row visible while scrolling.
Sort (Data tab) — arranges rows in ascending (A→Z, smallest→largest) or descending order, e.g. rank students by total.
Filter — shows only the rows that match, e.g. only students of Section B or only those above 80%.

Presentation software creates a set of slides with text, pictures, charts, audio and video to explain an idea to an audience. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx), LibreOffice Impress, Google Slides, Canva.

items.html: New slide — Home → New Slide (Ctrl + M) and choose a layout (Title Slide, Title and Content, Two Content, Picture with Caption).
Design — choose a theme for consistent colours and fonts.
Content — type in placeholders; insert pictures, icons, tables, charts, SmartArt, audio and video from the Insert tab.
Transitions (Transitions tab) — effects when one slide changes to the next (Fade, Push, Wipe).
Animations (Animations tab) — effects on objects within a slide (Appear, Fly In, Zoom), with entrance, emphasis and exit types.
Slide Show — F5 starts from the beginning; Shift + F5 from the current slide; Esc ends.

rows: Editing one slide at a time with thumbnails on the left
See all slides as small pictures; drag to rearrange
Preview the show inside a window

items.html: Follow the 6 × 6 rule: no more than six bullet points per slide and about six words per bullet.
Use large, readable fonts (at least 24 pt) and good contrast.
One idea per slide; use pictures and charts instead of long text.
Use transitions and animations sparingly — they should help, not distract.
Practise and speak to the audience; do not read the slides.

A spreadsheet arranges data in rows and columns; a workbook holds worksheets; a cell is addressed as column letter + row number.
Formulas start with = and follow BODMAS. Functions such as SUM, AVERAGE, MAX, MIN, COUNT, ROUND and IF save time.
Relative references change when copied; absolute references ($A$1 ) stay fixed.
Data can be formatted, sorted, filtered and shown as column, line, pie or scatter charts.
Presentation software makes slides with layouts, themes, media, transitions and animations; F5 starts the slide show.
